Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 13:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: define pen-test boundaries + evidence runbook (MSA / Order Form redlines)

Marta — thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers up front: ephemeral VPN + a timeboxed jumpbox session (audit-logged) is our preferred approach; we can reserve staging-only access for tests that require it but we'd prefer scoped ephemeral access overall.

On test types, Redwood will accept: 
- external network scanning (non-invasive)
- authenticated web app testing (credentialed, with agreed test accounts)
- internal network testing only when performed in an isolated staging environment
We do not permit social-engineering / phishing tests against production personnel.

72-hour blackout for operational incidents: we can agree to a 72-hour mutually-notified blackout window post-incident discovery where no scheduled pen-tests will occur. We propose adding a short clause to the Order Form that references incident notification procedures.

I attached a one-page runbook and a redline proposal for the Order Form that highlights: scope carveouts, evidence cadence (weekly sample sets during onboarding, then quarterly sampling), log retention windows for audit (45 days raw, 12 months aggregated), and an Operational Access checklist. 

Ben / Laura / Karthik — please review the attached redline and call out any legal or commercial items that need changes before I send back to Marta.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Manager, Security & Assurance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Evidence_Runbook_v1.2.pdf (PDF, 1 page), OrderForm-redline-proposed-20261213.docx (Word, tracked changes)

Soojin — good start. A few suggested edits inline to the redline (high level):
- Add an explicit definition of "inspection" versus "forensic access" so we don't conflate live production access with forensic downloads.
- Limit privileged session duration to a 4-hour maximum unless there's an approved extension request form. That helps ops scheduling.
- For pen-tests, require advance written notice 7 business days and a point-of-contact on both sides for kill-switch authority.

Laura / Karthik — flagged two legal points: the evidence cadence wording implies monthly deliverables for large customers; we should scope that to "onboarding" only to avoid perpetual monthly obligations that affect cost. Karthik, can you draft a short legal-friendly sentence to replace the onboarding paragraph?

If we all agree, I'll accept and push to Marta with the tracked changes.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: define pen-test boundaries + evidence runbook (MSA / Order Form redlines)

Team — drafted language below you can drop into the Order Form redline under "Assurance & Inspection". Keep it tight to avoid opening broad recurring obligations: 

"During an initial onboarding period (up to thirty (30) days following activation of the Service), Customer may request an evidence delivery cadence not to exceed monthly for the duration of onboarding. After onboarding, evidence deliveries will transition to quarterly spot samples unless otherwise agreed in writing. Inspection access will be limited to timeboxed, audit-logged sessions; forensic data exports are subject to prior written approval and a separate data transfer agreement. Penetration testing must be scheduled with at least seven (7) business days' notice, limited to the test types specified in the Security Exhibit, and may be paused for up to seventy-two (72) hours following discovery of an operational incident to allow remediation. Social-engineering tests are expressly excluded from permitted penetration testing activities."
I also tightened the privileged session duration wording to a default 4 hours; extension requires approval from Redwood security with a documented escalation. On the privileged access carveout: include a sentence that staging environments must be used for internal network testing; production internal scans require separate approval and a written justification.

Laura — happy to take the redline through legal review once you OK this wording.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
